hypothesis: Deep learning-based weather forecasting systems such as Pangu-Weather and GraphCast, which can accurately predict atmospheric variables including temperature, precipitation, and extreme weather events at high spatial resolution, hold strong potential to improve agricultural yield prediction by providing timely and precise weather forecasts that capture crop-relevant meteorological factors. These AI-based models have already surpassed traditional numerical weather prediction (NWP) methods in forecast accuracy across all weather variables and time ranges, and their fast inference speed enables real-time downstream applications—including scenarios directly relevant to agriculture such as drought, flood, and extreme temperature forecasting. As these deep learning frameworks continue to incorporate more observational factors and deeper network architectures, their integration into agricultural decision-support systems could substantially enhance the accuracy of yield predictions that depend on weather inputs.
